We got list of templates, but they seem unrelated (contain Br, etc). Need the correct template for intramolecular Michael addition cyclization. The search criteria may be too narrow; maybe need to include bonds formed/broken. The returned templates have low similarity. We need to find the one that matches our reaction. Could try to search without functional groups broken/formed, just bonds formed: C-C and C-O formed, C-O broken. Use bonds_formed list maybe "6-6" etc? Not sure.

Maybe easier: The template ID might be known from dataset. Could search with functional groups formed: ["ether oxygens"], broken: ["aromatic hydroxyls", "ketones"], bonds formed: ["C-C", "C-O"], bonds broken: ["C-O"]. But tool expects bond types like "6-6". Not sure.

Alternative: Use search without criteria, just limit 10, then manually inspect for a template that looks like intramolecular Michael addition. Look at retro_smarts_template fields. The first template: '[C:2]-[CH;D3;+0:1](-[C:3]=[O;D1;H0:4])-[O;H0;D2;+0:5]-[c:6]>>Br-[CH;D3;+0:1](-[C:2])-[C:3]=[O;D1;H0:4].[OH;D1;+0:5]-[c:6]' That's a forward reaction: product is C-O-aryl etc. Not our.

Second template: '[C:6]-[O;H0;D2;+0:7]-[c;H0;D3;+0:1](:[c:2]):[c:3]-[C:4]=[O;D1;H0:5]>>O-[c;H0;D3;+0:1](:[c:2]):[c:3]-[C:4]=[O;D1;H0:5].[C:6]-[OH;D1;+0:7]' This looks like cleavage of C-O bond to give phenol and carbonyl? Might be similar.

Our reaction: intramolecular cyclization: substrate chalcone has carbonyl (ketone) and alkene; product flavanone has carbonyl (still) and ether O (ring). So forward reaction (product to reactants) would be opening the ether to give phenol and carbonyl? Actually retrosynthetic step: break C-O ether to give phenol and carbonyl? The template likely breaks C-O bond and forms carbonyl? The second template seems to break C-O (ether) to give phenol and carbonyl? It has product side: O-aryl and carbonyl? The retro template: [C:6]-[O;H0;D2;+0:7]-[c...]>> O-aryl + [C:6]-[OH] (i.e., phenol + carbonyl?). That matches: break ether O to give phenol (aryl OH) and carbonyl (ketone). So template_id maybe 279112 (reaction_id). The template_id required is the one used to search the database not the hash. The template_id likely corresponds to reaction_id? The description says template_id (the one used to search the database not the hash). In search results, each entry has 'reaction_id' and 'template_hash'. Probably template_id is reaction_id. So we can return template_id 279112 and mapped_rxn from that entry.

We need mapped_rxn associated with the template that reproduces the reaction. The mapped_rxn field in entry is a long string with atom mapping. For template 279112, mapped_rxn is given. Let's extract it.

From result entry 2: 'mapped_rxn': 'CC(C)OC(=O)N=NC(=O)OC(C)C.C1=CC=C(P(C2=CC=CC=C2)C2=CC=CC=C2)C=C1.[O:18]=[C:17]([C:19]1=[CH:20][CH:21]=[CH:22][CH:23]=[CH:24]1)[C:16]1=[C:15](O)[CH:36]=[C:27]([O:28][CH2:29][C:30]2=[CH:31][CH:32]=[CH:33][N:34]=[CH:35]2)[CH:26]=[CH:25]1.[CH3:1][C:2]1=[C:3]([CH:4]([OH:14])[CH2:5][CH2:6][C:7](=[O:8])[O:9][C:10]([CH3:11])([CH3:12])[CH3:13])[CH:37]=[CH:38][CH:39]=[CH:40]1.C1CCOC1>>[CH3:1][C:2]1=[C:3]([CH:4]([CH2:5][CH2:6][C:7](=[O:8])[O:9][C:10]([CH3:11])([CH3:12])[CH3:13])[O:14][C:15]2=[C:16]([C:17](=[O:18])[C:19]3=[CH:20][CH:21]=[CH:22][CH:23]=[CH:24]3)[CH:25]=[CH:26][C:27]([O:28][CH2:29][C:30]3=[CH:31][CH:32]=[CH:33][N:34]=[CH:35]3)=[CH:36]2)[CH:37]=[CH:38][CH:39]=[CH:40]1'

That's huge and includes many extra fragments (maybe side reagents). Might be messy.

But maybe the correct template is 279112. Let's verify if this template matches our product SMILES. Use check_smiles_reaction_template_matching with product SMILES and template_id 279112.
We need to call check_smiles_reaction_template_matching.
